source_meta._title: /return executed within an advancement reward function globally discards all subsequent commands

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.20.3 Pre-Release 2 in a fresh single-player world using the integrated server, with commands enabled and the attached mc-266968.zip data pack installed. Execute the reproduction command from in-game chat as the player, not from a server console, because the data pack commands use @s.
preconditions: Obtain the report attachment named mc-266968.zip; keep it as a ZIP file and do not edit its functions or advancement files.
Configure the Minecraft Launcher to run exactly Minecraft Java Edition 1.20.3 Pre-Release 2, not the fixed version 1.20.3 Pre-Release 4.
Use a fresh, disposable world so that no unrelated data packs, functions, or advancement state can affect the reproduction.
Ensure commands are enabled for the world. The single-player procedure below uses Creative mode with Allow Commands enabled.
Use the default chat control T where stated, or the player's rebound Open Chat control if T has been changed.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation for exactly Java Edition 1.20.3 Pre-Release 2, launch it, and wait for the main menu to finish loading. Do not select 1.20.3 Pre-Release 4, because that is listed as the fix version rather than an affected version.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is visible and its version label identifies 1.20.3 Pre-Release 2.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, then Create New World. Give the world the unique name MC-266968-repro, select Creative game mode, set Allow Commands to ON, and create the world.
steps.success_cue: The new world begins loading with Creative mode and command access configured.

steps.action: Wait after entering the world until the surrounding terrain has rendered and normal player movement responds without world-loading delay.
steps.success_cue: The player can move normally in the loaded world and the nearby terrain is visible.

steps.action: Press Esc, select Save and Quit to Title, and wait until the main menu reappears. This closes the world before its data-pack directory is modified.
steps.success_cue: The main menu is visible and the MC-266968-repro world is no longer open.

steps.action: Using the operating system's file manager, open the game directory used by this launcher installation. Open saves, then the folder for MC-266968-repro, then datapacks. Copy the attached mc-266968.zip file directly into that datapacks directory without changing its filename or contents. If the launcher profile specifies a custom Game Directory, use that directory instead of the operating system's default .minecraft directory.
steps.success_cue: mc-266968.zip is present directly inside the MC-266968-repro world's datapacks directory.

steps.action: Return to Minecraft, select Singleplayer, select MC-266968-repro, and choose Play Selected World. Wait until terrain is rendered and player movement and commands respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is back in MC-266968-repro and the world has completed its initial loading.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Type the data-pack status command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter. This is only a setup verification and must be executed from in-game chat.
steps.success_cue: The enabled data-pack list includes the attached pack, normally identified by an entry containing file/mc-266968.zip. If it is absent or reported as invalid, stop before the trigger and correct the installation.

steps.action: Ensure the world has returned to normal player control after the verification command. Keep the player inside the world; do not switch to a server console, command block, or other execution context, because the reproduction function operates on the executing player through @s.
steps.success_cue: The player is active in the world with command permission, and mc-266968.zip has been confirmed as enabled.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat again.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open at the bottom of the screen.

steps.action: Enter the report's function command exactly as written, including the leading slash. Do not press Enter yet.
steps.success_cue: The complete text /function mc-266968:a is present in the in-game chat input field and is ready to be submitted.

steps.action: Press Enter once to submit and execute /function mc-266968:a as the player. Do not run it repeatedly; immediately hand control to the observation subsystem after this single execution.
steps.success_cue: The command has been submitted, function execution has completed or returned control to the player, and the resulting chat output is available for immediate inspection.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just executed /function mc-266968:a once from in-game chat in the affected version, with mc-266968.zip enabled. Begin observing the resulting command-generated chat output before executing any additional command.
uncertainties: The report does not specify single-player versus dedicated-server execution, game mode, world seed, or coordinates. This plan uses a fresh Creative single-player world with commands enabled because it supplies a player execution context for @s without adding unrelated server conditions.

The attachment contents themselves were not included as an accessible file in the supplied report text. The plan assumes the attachment named mc-266968.zip is the directly installable data pack referenced by the report and should be placed unchanged in the world's datapacks directory.
The displayed enabled-pack identifier can vary slightly in formatting, but it should clearly correspond to mc-266968.zip.
No external web verification was needed because the supplied report provides the affected version, attachment name, namespace, function command, and relevant data-pack resources.
